py-program.def: A list of instructions Python carries out one line at a time, top to bottom.

py-operator.def: A symbol that combines values: + - * / // % **, comparisons such as == and <.

py-variable.def: A name tied to a value so you can use it later, created with = (read "gets").

py-assignment.def: name = value: work out the right side, then tie the name on the left to it. It never copies.

py-type.def: The kind of a value, which decides what you can do with it: int, float, str, bool, list… Check with type(x).

py-method.def: A function that belongs to a value, called with a dot: name.upper(), marks.append(70).

py-fstring.def: Text with f before the quote; values in {…} are put in, optionally formatted, e.g. f"{x:.2f}".

py-list.def: An ordered, changeable collection of values in square brackets: [62, 75, 81].

py-index.def: The position of an item, counted from 0; negative indices count from the end (xs[-1] is the last).

py-slice.def: xs[start:stop:step]: the items from start up to but not including stop; it has stop − start items when step is 1.

py-loop.def: Repeats an indented block once for each item: for m in marks:.

py-function.def: A named machine defined with def: arguments go in, return hands a value back (or None without a return).

py-module.def: A file of ready-made Python tools that you import, e.g. math, statistics, numpy.

py-traceback.def: Python's error report. Read the last line (error type and reason) first, then the line number.
